title: From opinion to conviction, and meaning in the day
header_line: My analysis of one book on neuro-linguistic programming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What does your day mean to you?
A student said that when your environment is aligned with your goals you are congruent; if you say you want to be successful but are surrounded by people who are not, you are incongruent.
I said that what you say to others, such as we are kicking ass and we will make the calls, affects your beliefs sooner or later. An opinion matures into a belief and then a conviction.
I asked: can you grab something you do day to day and attach meaning to it: this means something to me, I enjoy what I am learning, I enjoy the process?
A student said that in a hard moment he made seventy-five calls in a parking lot to find a solution, because he was determined to get out of it.
Another said: this morning I was thinking about what motivates me, and it comes back to your goal.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write your environment and whether it matches your goal.
Write what you say aloud about your work.
Write whether it is an opinion, a belief or a conviction.
Write the meaning you attach to your day.

check.q: What did a student say about environment and goals?
What did I say an opinion becomes?
What did I ask you to attach to your day?

recap: Match your environment to your goal. Attach meaning to your day.
